anomalies.observed: The two 120R CAN termination resistors are wired to the wrong terminals of the 2-bit DIP switch SW8. SW8 switch 1 (pins 1-2) joins Net-(R102-Pad2) and Net-(R36-Pad2) (the free ends of R102 and R36, which sit on the CAN_L sides of the two buses), while SW8 switch 2 (pins 3-4) joins /NET0001 (U38 CANH, bus 1) directly to /NET0050 (U22 CANH, bus 0). R102.1 is on /NET0164 (U22 CANL) and R36.1 is on /NET0142 (U38 CANL).
anomalies.expected: Per the spec the board has two independent CAN buses (CAN0/CAN1). Each 120R termination resistor should be placed across CAN_H and CAN_L of its own bus (R102 between /NET0050 and /NET0164; R36 between /NET0001 and /NET0142), and the two buses must never be joined. Standard CAN practice also requires a 120R termination across each bus.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: With SW8 open neither CAN bus has any termination (signal reflections, marginal high-speed CAN). With SW8 closed the two supposedly independent buses are shorted together on CAN_H (and tied through 240R on CAN_L), destroying bus isolation/independence and still not providing correct 120R termination.

parsed.summary: The CAN termination/option DIP switch SW8 is miswired: its two poles join the two buses' CAN_H lines together and the two termination resistors' free ends together, instead of placing each 120R resistor across its own bus. This both prevents proper termination and, when the switch is closed, shorts the two intended-independent CAN buses together.

Actually LM2576's OUT pin is the switch node (the emitter of internal transistor). The catch diode anode is at ground, cathode at OUT pin. Yes that's standard. So D26 anode=GND, cathode=OUT/L2.
